title: Reorder List
statement:
Rearrange a singly linked list in place so it alternates between the front and the back.

Contract
- `head` may be null or may point to the first node of an acyclic list. Each node has an integer `value` and a mutable `next` reference.
- A list `L0 -> L1 -> ... -> Ln` must become `L0 -> Ln -> L1 -> Ln-1 -> L2 -> ...`, ending when every node has been used once.
- The method returns nothing: the original head node stays the head and the last node of the new order must have `next` equal to null.
- Relink the existing nodes. Do not allocate replacement nodes, change node values, or copy the nodes into an array or list.

Examples
- `1 -> 2 -> 3 -> 4` becomes `1 -> 4 -> 2 -> 3`.
- `1 -> 2 -> 3 -> 4 -> 5` becomes `1 -> 5 -> 2 -> 4 -> 3`.
- A one-node list stays unchanged.
hints: The back half is needed in reverse order, but a singly linked list cannot be walked backwards.
Find the middle with a slow and a fast pointer, cut the list there, and reverse the second half in place.
Interleave the two halves node by node, taking care to save each successor before relinking. Intended complexity: O(n) time and O(1) extra space, where n is the number of nodes.
inputSyntax: Input: the list values in order, for example: [1, 2, 3, 4]
